name: Shakti meditation prep: hippocampus right
origin: Todd Murphy, 8 Coil Shakti meditation recipe
summary: Murphy's meditation recipe for the 8 Coil Shakti, hippocampal variant: 30 min of the hippocampal signal over the right temporal lobe only, then meditate 60 to 120 min later. Murphy reports deeper meditation when the practice follows the session ('Shakti first, and the other an hour to 90 minutes later').
setting: No sensory deprivation needed; sit or lie relaxed. Do not meditate during the session. Practise (for example Vipassana or Zen) 60 to 120 min after it ends.
schedule: Murphy asks for patience: it may take several sessions. Vendor rules: at most once a week or every 72 h, never on consecutive days; a series of up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: Murphy: for Vipassana or Zen use Feelgood or 'altered states' sessions over both sides, or hippocampal signals over the right side only, and 30 min is 'the right length for meditation enhancement'. This file is the right-side hippocampal variant, on the 8 Coil Shakti's 4-coil cross over the right temporal lobe (front FT8, top C6, back TP8, bottom T10; the vendor gives the cross as a chart and photos without 10-10 names, so the sites are an inference); the left channels stay silent. The Feelgood and Altered States options are separate programs and are not copied here: murphy-shakti8-feelgood-1phase-frontal (30 min) or murphy-shakti8-feelgood-2phase-40min, and murphy-shakti8-altered-states-40min; end them 60 to 120 min before meditating. The wait and the meditation are not part of the program; use your own timer. The hippocampal 'LTP' file is proprietary. It is approximated on the vendor's standard 3-ms points: 4 bursts of 4 biphasic pulses 9 ms apart, one burst every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal), then the standard 4 s of silence (about 9.4 s of field per minute; the vendor gives 9.6 s). Hippocampus on the right follows a small Persinger-lab study (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: right-sided LTP-pattern fields were rated more pleasant). Murphy warns that meditating or using another mind machine during the session 'gives your brain conflicting instructions'; he also says a session can strengthen other mind machines used about 2 h later, and the vendor limits use to 'three to five devices per day'. The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop at once on fear or any distress. Independent double-blind tests found no effect of God-Helmet-type fields (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
